body:
## Pull request overview

This PR redesigns the playground UI following the play.tailwindcss.com aesthetic with a collapsible editor panel and responsive preview modes. The changes focus on improving the user experience with smooth transitions, device-specific preview capabilities, and visual enhancements using gradients and backdrop blur effects.

**Changes:**
- Added collapsible editor panel with localStorage persistence and SSR safety guards
- Implemented responsive preview modes (desktop/tablet/mobile) with icon-based toggle controls
- Enhanced visual aesthetics with gradient backgrounds, backdrop blur effects, and smooth animations
- Removed unused plugin imports from ObjectUIProvider to improve performance

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/site/app/playground/page.tsx | Added collapsible editor functionality, responsive preview modes, visual enhancements with gradients and transitions, and improved Monaco editor configuration |
| apps/site/app/components/ObjectUIProvider.tsx | Removed unused plugin imports that are not needed in the playground (plugins are loaded separately in InteractiveDemo component where needed) |

Missing explicit type="button" attribute. Buttons should explicitly specify type="button" to prevent them from acting as submit buttons if they're ever placed inside a form context. This is a best practice to make the intent clear and prevent potential bugs.
```suggestion
          <button
            type="button"
```

Missing explicit type="button" attribute on example selector buttons. Buttons should explicitly specify type="button" to prevent them from acting as submit buttons if they're ever placed inside a form context. This is a best practice to make the intent clear and prevent potential bugs.
```suggestion
                      key={key}
                      type="button"
```

Mixing inline styles with Tailwind transitions can cause conflicts. The overflow property is being animated via inline styles while transition-all on line 326 applies to all CSS properties. This violates the coding guideline that forbids inline styles (style={{}}) and requires using Tailwind CSS utilities exclusively. Consider using Tailwind's overflow utilities with conditional classes instead of inline styles.

Inline styles are forbidden according to the coding guidelines which require exclusive use of Tailwind CSS utilities. The dynamic left position should be implemented using Tailwind's arbitrary values or dynamic classes. The transition-all on line 366 will attempt to animate this inline style property, which can cause performance issues and conflicts with Tailwind's transition system.

Inline styles violate the coding guidelines which forbid style={{}} and require exclusive use of Tailwind CSS utilities. The dynamic width should be implemented using Tailwind's arbitrary values or by creating a CSS variable. The transition-all on line 418 will animate this inline style, but mixing inline styles with Tailwind transitions can cause conflicts and performance issues.

Missing explicit type="button" attribute on button elements. In React, buttons inside forms default to type="submit" which can cause unintended form submissions. While this playground page doesn't have a form, it's a best practice to always explicitly set type="button" on interactive buttons to prevent future issues and make the intent clear.
```suggestion
                      key={mode}
                      type="button"
```
